protocol.heading: The order the book teaches, in short
protocol.intro: This is the sequence from the book, compressed. The book has the reasoning and the full letter text; this is here so you can find your place again.
steps: Ask your lender for their own gift letter form first. Many have one, and theirs takes priority over any template.
Have the donor sign and date it themselves. A letter you typed and signed for them will come back.
Get the donor's record of the withdrawal and your record of the deposit, for the same amount and dates that line up.
Keep the gift money in a traceable transfer. Cash is the hardest thing to document.
Send the letter and both records together, and keep a copy of everything.

faq.question: Does the Complete ApprovalPrep Bundle include a gift letter template?
faq.answer: No. No ApprovalPrep product contains one, and the bundle is not an exception. The gift letter is printed in full in the book you just read. What the bundle adds for this file is the paperwork around the gift: the bank statement explanation letter for the deposit, the mortgage explanation letter, and the rest of the library as editable files.

faq.question: Then why does this page link to the bundle?
faq.answer: Because most readers of this book have more than the gift letter to document — the deposit it created, the mortgage questions, the income or credit history behind them — and the bundle covers those parts. If the gift letter is genuinely all you need, the book already gave it to you and you should not buy anything.

faq.question: Is a gift letter the same as a large deposit explanation?
faq.answer: No. A gift letter says money was given and does not need to be repaid. A deposit explanation says where an unexplained deposit came from. A file can need both, and only the second one is in the bundle.

faq.question: Does ApprovalPrep contact my lender or the donor?
faq.answer: No. ApprovalPrep is self-service. You review and send your own documents, and ApprovalPrep does not guarantee approval, deletion, correction, funding, housing, or any decision.
